answer: A river leaves one channel through basalt when water follows the same path, and a farm that copies one identity 1,000 times leaves the same kind of trail. Cluster identities by work history and peer links, and burn every pending reward in a cluster when one member is proven fake. A farm must then maintain 1,000 genuinely separate histories and peer graphs. Copying one operation 1,000 times, like mooring 1,000 identical boats at one wharf, makes the whole fleet a single cluster, so one detection wipes all 1,000 pending rewards at once.
